author: CC
at_sea: Research boundary, no voyage in flight and no code moved. Akien's question — what makes a good persistent chatbot, who leads, which levers matter, how do we do better BEFORE tuning the librarian — was answered by three parallel research sweeps (consumer / infrastructure / academic) synthesized against the librarian as built through ticket the-tenure-loop. The durable record is CairnCommons/notes/2026-08-10-persistent-chatbot-field-survey.json (commons 4cfd601, pushed): three camps (summarize-and-stuff, memory-is-context-engineering, graph extraction) plus the librarian as a fourth (answer-from-structure, nobody else does it); levers ranked by evidence — reflection/consolidation d=8.16 the biggest, update/invalidation the step production memory measurably loses on (97.8% junk audits, 91.6%→49% staleness collapse), forgetting improves accuracy, temporal reasoning the sharpest replicated differentiator, proactive callbacks +8.3pp; benchmark ecosystem LOW-TRUST (tune dials against our own armed probe, never field numbers). Where we stand: the tenure loop sits exactly on the field's #1 production failure; the uncast ladder rungs (warm set, self tree, consolidation) map blind onto the field's biggest levers; honest gaps are contradiction/invalidation (an earned node gone WRONG has no path), pure-cosine walk, no proactive surface. Akien's 'ask me again' vs 'I have something new' resolved as two moments of ONE mechanism — the promotion/resolution event that already fires IS the callback trigger.
